types/utils.ts/Overwrite: only overwrite keys of objects

Overwrite<string,string> resulted in a mangled object type
because the existing implementation iterated over the string
type's keys (e.g. 'charCodeAt')

This commit changes the implementation so that keys are only
iterated and overwritten in the case of objects. Otherwise,
a non-never TWith type will entirely replace TType, e.g.
Overwrite<string, number> results in 'number'.

summary.intent: Fix the inferred input type of procedures whose `.input()` parser yields a primitive and is followed by `.use()` middleware, by making the internal `Overwrite` type merge key-wise only when both operands are objects and otherwise replace the left operand with the right one; add a regression test.
summary.issue_fit: Issue alignment unavailable: the PR body is the unfilled template (`Closes #` empty) and the packet names no originating issue, so intent comes from the PR title, the message of commit 7dc04a7, and review thread 4 of the supplied PR text. Every ledger row is met, and the compatibility disposition of the `Overwrite` promise is violated only for nullish context overwrites (finding). The regression test is named after issue #5020, which was not supplied; whether it reports further input shapes is the open question.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed in full, with every `Overwrite` consumer (core/middleware.ts, core/internals/procedureBuilder.ts, core/internals/utils.ts), the public export path (internals.ts, index.ts), the runtime context merge in procedureBuilder.ts, and the regression tests for issues 2856, 4321, 4527, 4947 plus smoke.test.ts. The whole tests package type-checked at head. Untracked `.mcp.json` in the working tree is outside the committed range and was not reviewed.

Reviewer ran scratch tsc configurations under the work directory (`review-MtiV2o/scratch`): unit.ts compares copied merge-base and head `Overwrite` definitions (errors only at the two deliberate probes, lines 46 and 62); e2e.ts against the head source errs at lines 46 and 54 and against a copy of the merge-base `packages/server/src` errs at lines 42, 43, 46 and 53, so the `strWithMiddleware` input and output assertions fail at the merge-base and hold at head; line 46 is an optional-object probe whose expectation omitted `void` and is not evidence for any item; probe2.ts shows an optional-object input through middleware accepts a string literal at the merge-base and is `{ q: string } | undefined` at head.

Verifier batches re-ran those configurations and added their own (`verifier-scratch/unit2.ts`, `e2e2.ts`; `verifier-scratch-2/unit3.ts`, `unit4.ts`, `cross.ts`, `cross2.ts`), including a two-version program comparing head and merge-base `@trpc/server` types through every `Overwrite` consumer.

The vitest runtime suite was not run: the run policy names tsc as the discriminating check for this type-only change, and `expectTypeOf` assertions are no-ops at runtime. No CI check evidence was supplied.

findings.title: Keep the previous context when a middleware overwrites it with a nullish value
findings.trigger: A middleware returns `opts.next({ ctx: cond ? { user } : undefined })`, or passes a `| null` value, and a later middleware or the resolver reads a field of `ctx`.
findings.impact: At the merge-base the downstream `ctx` type was `{ ...prev, user } | prev`, matching the runtime merge `{ ...callOpts.ctx, ...nextOpts.ctx }`, which never yields a nullish value; at head it is `{ ...prev, user } | undefined`, so reads that compiled before now fail with TS18048/TS18047 although runtime behaviour is unchanged. Only nullable context overwrites are affected.
findings.change: In the non-object `TWith` arms of `Overwrite` (lines 21-24 and 26-29), return `TType` when the distributed `TWith` member is `null` or `undefined`, for example `TWith extends null | undefined ? TType : TWith`, or document that nullish context overwrites are unsupported.
findings.source: Commit 7dc04a7, "a non-never TWith type will entirely replace TType"; released `@trpc/server` 10.43.2 exports `Overwrite` from its root via src/internals.ts.

findings.title: Remove the unreachable `: TType` arm and fix the `never` doc sentence
findings.trigger: A reader of the exported `Overwrite` type relies on the comment "unless TWith is never" or on the `: TType` arm to expect `TType` back for a `never` overwrite.
findings.impact: `TWith extends any ? TWith : TType` distributes over the naked parameter, so a `never` argument becomes `never` before either arm is chosen: `Overwrite<string, never>` and `Overwrite<{ a: 1 }, never>` are both `never`, the arm is dead, and the sibling arm at line 24 already says `never` for the same case. The comment and code describe behaviour the type does not have.
findings.change: Collapse lines 25-29 to `: TWith` and reword lines 8-9 to say a `never` `TWith` yields `never`; if `TType` is intended for `never`, use the non-distributive check `[TWith] extends [never] ? TType : TWith` instead.

questions.title: Which input shapes does issue #5020 report, and are they all covered?
questions.evidence: The regression test is named `issue-5020-inference-middleware.test.ts`, but the PR body's `Closes #` is empty and the packet lists no originating issue, so the issue text was not available. The demonstrated merge-base to head changes are: a primitive input followed by `.use()` now infers the parser type (`string`) instead of a mapped object over `String.prototype` keys; an optional object input followed by `.use()` now infers `{ ... } | undefined` instead of a union widened by `{}` that accepted any non-nullish value; a nullish `next({ ctx })` overwrite now infers `| undefined` (finding). Array and tuple inputs through middleware are mapped key-wise at both versions and are unchanged.
questions.why_it_matters: The issue defines the acceptance set for this fix. If every reported shape is among the demonstrated changes, the ledger closes as met and the decision becomes Approved with the two consider findings; a reported shape outside them would add a partial requirement row and reopen as a requirement finding.
questions.answer: The maintainers or the orchestrator supply the text of issue #5020 (and link it from the PR body). Its reported shapes are compared against the three demonstrated changes above.
